name: Deferred Jump Hedge
note: Baltussen et al. find intraday jumps predict returns but that the hedge lands at the close, because partial hedging under fixed costs defers the residual to where depth is. Detects a jump (|5-min log return| >= k x the trailing 20-session median absolute return) between 10:00 and 14:30 ET, cancels the day if a later jump reverses sign, then opens IN THE JUMP'S DIRECTION at 15:30 ET and exits on the close. Signal and entry are deliberately decoupled by hours.
source: Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (2021), JFE 142(1), 377-403 - 'we do find evidence that large price jumps during the day predict subsequent returns... the bulk of the hedge seems to take place towards the end of the day', citing Clewlow & Hodges (1997) on partial hedging under fixed costs.
